ops.title: synckit + captain-hook: migrate off service.LimitLoadToSessionType before daemonkit deletes it
ops.description:
daemonkit deprecated `Agent.LimitLoadToSessionType`, `SessionType`, its five constants and `ParseSessionType` in the v0.21.0 remediation release: **accepted and ignored, no longer rendered into the plist**. The symbols are deleted in the Phase-3 breaking release, which carries the coordinated repin sweep.

**Why it is going away (measured in Phase 0).** launchd refuses any job whose session type names a domain other than the bootstrap domain's own — error 134, *"Service cannot load in requested session"*. daemonkit hard-codes `domainTarget()` to `gui/<uid>`. So `Aqua` was always a **measured no-op**, and every other value was a **guaranteed permanent refusal**. The key never did anything except break agents.

**This is why the daemonkit change is a bug fix, not just a deprecation:** a consumer asking for `Background` currently ships an agent launchd permanently refuses. Once the key is not emitted, that agent loads.

## Owed work, per repo

**synckit** — `daemon/service.go` sets `helper.LimitLoadToSessionType` and carries `serviceSessionType(manifest.SessionType) (dkservice.SessionType, error)` mapping all five constants. The hard part is that this is backed by a **user-facing manifest field** (`manifest.SessionTypeAqua`, `manifest.SessionTypeBackground`, …), so the migration is a product decision, not a mechanical edit: is the manifest key rejected, ignored with a warning, or removed? Note that any manifest specifying a non-`Aqua` value describes an agent that has never worked, so "ignored with a warning" is the honest reading and matches what daemonkit now does.

**captain-hook** — `internal/hookd/deployment.go` sets `LimitLoadToSessionType: service.SessionTypeAqua` on both agents (trivially deletable — `Aqua` is the measured no-op) and separately carries `deploymentServicePolicy.SessionType service.SessionType` with tag `json:"session_type"`. That second one is a **serialized signed-deployment-policy schema**, so removing it is a schema migration with its own archive-or-migrate decision.

**cc-notes** — nothing to do in cc-notes itself. It fails fleet-build only through the *released* module `fusekit@v1.15.4` in the module cache; fusekit's local checkout has already migrated off. It clears when fusekit cuts a release built against the new daemonkit and cc-notes bumps its pin.

**Not in scope:** cc-present's fleet-build failure is unrelated and pre-existing — a `synckit@v0.31.0` pin calling `workers.ClaimRuntime()` with no arguments against `worker.ClaimRuntime(worker.VerifierBudgets)`.

## Sequencing

These land in the consumer repos while daemonkit is still accepting-and-ignoring the field, so there is no lockstep and no flag day. Only after all three are clear does the Phase-3 deletion become invisible to `scripts/fleet-build.sh` — and the standing rule is **fleet-build red = no release, ever**.

ops.text: synckit no longer references dkservice.SessionType or LimitLoadToSessionType, and its manifest session-type key has a decided disposition (rejected / ignored-with-warning / removed)
captain-hook drops the LimitLoadToSessionType agent literals and has a migration or archive path for the serialized session_type policy field
fusekit has cut a release built against post-deprecation daemonkit and cc-notes has bumped its pin
scripts/fleet-build.sh in daemonkit is green except for cc-present's unrelated pre-existing failure
